[[File:Embedding space.png|thumbnail|350px|Each dimension of an '''embedding space''' encodes some semantic meaning. As such, words with similar meanings are spatially adjacent to each other.]]
[[File:Token embedding 2.png|thumbnail|350px|Since each dimension encodes some semantic meaning, vector addition/subtraction can add/extract meaning to tokens and relate them to other tokens.]]
== Embedding and unembedding [[function]]s ==

Let $t_i \in \mathcal{T}$ be [[token (machine learning)|token]]s obtained from [[tokenisation (machine learning)|tokenisation]] of raw data.

Let $\mathbb{E}\equiv \mathbb{R}^d$ be a [[vector space]].

Then '''vector embedding function'''

$$
\operatorname{E}: \mathcal{T} \to \mathbb{E}\\
\forall t_i \in \mathcal{T}: t_i \mapsto \vec{e}_i
$$

$\mathbb{E}$ is then known as the $d$-dimensional '''embedding space''' of $\operatorname{E}$, which contains '''embedding vectors''' $\vec e_i$.

Similarly,

$$
\operatorname{U}: \mathbb{E} \to \mathcal{T} \\
\forall \vec e_i \in \mathbb{E}: \vec e_i \mapsto t_i
$$

is the '''unembedding function'''.

== Matrix representation ==

=== Embedding matrix ===

Let $\mathbf{W}_E \in \mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{V}| \times d}$ be a '''vector embedding matrix'''.

$$
\vec{e}_i = \mathbf{W}_E[t_i].
$$

=== Unembedding matrix ===

Let $\vec o$ denote the output vector.

Let $\mathbf{W}_U \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times |\mathcal{V}|}$ be a '''vector unembedding matrix'''.

$$
\mathrm{logits} = \vec o \mathbf{W}_U.
$$

<blockquote>
Frequently, one sets $\mathbf{W}_U=\mathbf{W}_E^T$, a practice known as '''weight-tying'''.
</blockquote>

== Example ==

{{Hidden example}}
'''Setup'''

* Vocabulary size $|\mathcal{V}|=4$
** Tokens: <code>cat</code>, <code>dog</code>, <code>fish</code>, and <code>bird</code>
* Embedding dimension: $d=3$

'''Embedding matrix $\mathbf{W}_E$''' (shape $4 \times 3$):

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! !! dim1 !! dim2 !! dim3
|-
| <code>cat</code> || $0.2$ || $0.5$ || $-0.1$
|-
| <code>dog</code> || $-0.3$ || $0.1$ || $0.4$
|-
| <code>fish</code> || $0.6$ || $-0.2$ || $0.3$
|-
| <code>bird</code> || $-0.1$ || $0.4$ || $0.2$
|}

'''Unembedding matrix (weight-tied) $\mathbf{W}_U = \mathbf{W}_E^\top$''' (shape $3 \times 4$):

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! !! <code>cat</code> !! <code>dog</code> !! <code>fish</code> !! <code>bird</code>
|-
| dim1 || $0.2$ || $-0.3$ || $0.6$ || $-0.1$
|-
| dim2 || $0.5$ || $0.1$ || $-0.2$ || $0.4$
|-
| dim3 || $-0.1$ || $0.4$ || $0.3$ || $0.2$
|}


'''Embedding'''

Embed <code>cat</code>

$$
\vec e_1 = \mathbf{W}_E[1]=[0.2,\ 0.5,\ -0.1]
$$

'''Unembedding'''

Suppose after some operations, one obtains $\vec o=[-0.42,0.15,0.41]$.

Compute logits:

$$
\vec \ell = \vec o \mathbf{W}_U \\
= [-0.42,\ 0.15,\ 0.41] \begin{bmatrix} 0.2 & -0.3 & 0.6 & -0.1 \\ 0.5 & 0.1 & -0.2 & 0.4 \\ -0.1 & 0.4 & 0.3 & 0.2 \end{bmatrix} = [-0.05,\ 0.305,\ -0.159,\ 0.184].
$$

<blockquote>
With a weight-tied $\mathbf{W}_U$, unembedding is essentially calculating the [[vector dot product]]s $\ell_i$ of output $\vec o$ with the embedding vectors $\mathbf{W}_E[i]$ for each [[token]] $t_i$ in the vocabulary. As $\vec o \cdot \mathbf{W}_E[i] = \| \vec o \| \| \mathbf{W}_E[i] \| \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec o$ and $\mathbf{W}_E[i]$, one expects $\ell_i$ to be larger when the directions of $\vec o$ and $\mathbf{W}_E[i]$ align, signifying a higher possibility the model's output predicts token $t_i$.
</blockquote>

Calculate [[softmax]] probabilities:

$$
\vec{p} = \text{softmax}(\vec{\ell}) \approx [0.218,\ 0.311,\ 0.196,\ 0.276].
$$

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Token !! Probability $p_j$
|-
| <code>cat</code> || $0.218$
|-
| <code>dog</code> || $0.311$
|-
| <code>fish</code> || $0.196$
|-
| <code>bird</code> || $0.276$
|}

Thus the model somehow transformed a cat into something that is between a cat, a dog, a fish, and a bird. 
{{End hidden}}
